stem: A retention policy calls for objects to move from S3 Standard to Standard-IA at 30 days, then to Glacier Flexible Retrieval at 45 days, then expire at 400 days, and a monthly bill shows early-transition charges the team did not expect.

choices.text: The transition to Glacier Flexible Retrieval was scheduled before Standard-IA's 30-day minimum storage duration elapsed
The 400-day expiration is longer than Glacier Flexible Retrieval's 90-day minimum storage duration
The rule filtered objects by tag instead of by prefix
The bucket's default 128 KB minimum object size blocked the transitions

rationale: Objects reach Standard-IA at day 30 and are scheduled to leave for Glacier Flexible Retrieval at day 45, only 15 days later, which is less than Standard-IA's 30-day minimum storage duration and triggers an early-transition charge. The 400-day expiration being longer than Glacier Flexible Retrieval's 90-day minimum is true, but a later expiration than a minimum duration does not cause a charge, so it is not the source of the problem described. Whether a rule filters by tag or by prefix does not change how minimum storage durations are enforced. The 128 KB default minimum size, if it applied here, would block a transition entirely rather than let it happen early and generate a charge.
